narrative.overview: A clinical memorial to AI-generated technical debt. The graveyard is a forensic record disguised as a website — obituary aesthetics for an absurd modern phenomenon. Monospace fonts, flat dark surfaces, one clinical red accent. The humor exists entirely in the gap between the serious format and the ridiculous content.
keyCharacteristics: Monospace-first typography — reads like a terminal report, not a webpage
Flat, zero-shadow surfaces — depth through tonal layering only
One accent color, ruthlessly constrained — red on ≤15% of any screen
Generous negative space — each entry breathes; sparse by design
Obituary aesthetic: clinical, darkly funny, surgical

rules.name: The Morgue Red Rule
rules.body: The accent appears on ≤15% of any given screen. Links, active states, and CTAs are the only permitted uses.

rules.name: The Monospace Majority Rule
rules.body: At least 70% of visible text is monospace. Sans-serif exists only for paragraph-length body copy.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: box-shadow does not exist in this design system. If a surface needs to feel elevated, make it lighter, not lifted.

dos: Do use monospace for all headings, labels, metadata, buttons, and UI chrome.
Do keep the accent red at ≤15% of any screen.
Do use tonal layering (void → surface → border) for depth, never shadows.
Do write entry descriptions in neutral, clinical language.
Do keep cards spacious: 1.25rem padding, 0.75rem gaps.
Do use uppercase + monospace for all labels and tags.
Do maintain the obituary aesthetic: sparse, serious, data-like.
donts: Don't use shadows, gradients, glassmorphism, or any decorative elevation.
Don't add a second accent color.
Don't make it look like a SaaS landing page.
Don't make it look like a tech blog.
Don't use aggressive or mocking language — we're the coroner, not the murderer.
Don't use sans-serif for headings or metadata.
Don't make it look like it was built with AI.
